Stawiski Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stawiski, Poland

Not demolished. Stawiski's Jewish community, first mentioned in the 17th century, formed a pre-kehilla by 1765 and a full kehilla at the start of the 19th century, reaching 1,920 people (63 percent of the town) by 1921, most killed during a 1941 pogrom and mass executions, or later at Treblinka. This cemetery, likely founded at the beginning of the 19th century, served as the burial site for local rabbis including Chaim Myszkowski and Aron Dworski, and sits atop the remains of an early medieval settlement with visible earthen embankments. In 2009, members of the Warsaw Jewish Community relocated some recovered tombstones due to recurring flooding, caused in part by local beaver dams.
